description: An interrupted conversation keeps the context count in place on phones. The page takes /c/interrupted's last turn for interrupted; /c/steady is an ordinary conversation. window.countAt() returns where the one visible token count (".context-usage-label-tokens") ends, as JSON [right, top], or what is wrong when there isn't exactly one; window.settledCountAt() is a promise of the same, read once no CSS transition is running (the phone composer's gap changes through a transition when the count arrives). "The group" is [data-testid="conversation-interrupted"]; "its message" is ".status-message" inside the group. Perform the steps in order. 1. For each width W of 1280, 390, 360 and 320 in turn: a. resize the viewport to W x 800 (set_viewport width and height only); b. navigate to /c/steady; c. there should be exactly one visible count: eval window.countAt().startsWith('[') with expect "true"; then save where it is across the navigation once transitions finish: eval, awaited, window.settledCountAt().then((at) => (sessionStorage.idle = at).startsWith('[')) with expect "true"; d. navigate to /c/interrupted; e. its message's innerText, trimmed, should be exactly "Conversation Interrupted" (eval with expect, failing if the message is missing); f. the resume button (data-testid "resume-interrupted-button") should be visible; g. the message must not overflow: eval its scrollWidth <= clientWidth with expect "true"; h. eval window.countAt().startsWith('[') with expect "true" (exactly one visible count); i. only when W is below 768 (phones keep the count in the composer row, where it is otherwise): once transitions finish, the count must be where it was in /c/steady, read once: eval, awaited, (window.__phoneAt ??= window.settledCountAt()).then((at) => at === sessionStorage.idle ? 'in place' : at + ' vs ' + sessionStorage.idle) with expect "in place" (the first reading is kept, so a retry of the eval cannot wait for the count to move back). 2. A failed Continue says so once, where errors otherwise show: the test server answers every resume request (POST /api/conversation/<id>/resume) with 503 "Resume failed", so there is nothing to set up. Click the resume button. 3. There should be exactly one ".status-error", with text exactly "Resume failed". 4. ".message-controls-status-slot .status-error" should be visible. 5. The group's count should be 0.
